# Committing and pushing

**scratch**
: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, probe programs, lists and private caches folders.

Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.

## What to commit

- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
- In a fresh clone, `.claude/worktrees/` and `.claude/agents/` show as untracked, because the lines of `.git/info/exclude` that hide them are not in the clone. Do not commit them.
- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, which is gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.

## How to commit

Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:

    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>

- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:

      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB

  If your brief gives another session line, use it. If a commit that is already made has a footer that names a model, by any name or identifier, leave the commit as it is. Such a footer is not a defect: do not check for it, report it or list it.

## Pushing

Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.

- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
- From a session in a cloud container, do not try to delete a branch on GitHub, or retry a refusal with another tool (the `cloud-container` skill, "Rules for every agent"). Removing a worktree does not delete its branch, which stays. Ask nobody in your report to delete a branch.
- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
  3. If it lists only your commits, push the three refs with this one command, and wait for it to end:

         git push --atomic origin main main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8 main:blinded-fable

     With `--atomic`, the three refs update together or not at all. Do not pipe the command into another command, since a pipe hides a refusal. A refusal shows as a line that starts with `!`, and as a non-zero exit. The last ref keeps `blinded-fable` current. If the container is lost, the platform rebuilds it from that branch.
- Push no branch that this section does not name, unless your brief names it.
- If a push is refused, push nothing more, and do not run it again. Report the refused ref and git's message.

# The gate

The gate runs the seven steps below on one tree, in about 25 minutes. It is green if every step passes, and red if one fails. If a step fails, run the rest, so that the summary holds every step's result.

## What it writes

The summary, `summary.txt`, has one tab-separated row for each suite: `track/suite`, tests, failures, errors, skipped. Below the rows, lines that start with `#` give each log's `BUILD` and `Total time:` lines, the machine that ran the gate (`# machine`), the atomic runs and the ladder's comparison. A landed summary can also end with `# microgpt-walk` lines: the `VERDICT:` and `rc=` lines of the microGPT walk check (`interpreter.md`, "The model program"), run on the landed tree. Add them only if your brief asks for the microGPT walk check on the landed tree.

If your brief asks you to land a gate's results, put them in a new `gate/` folder in `explorations/compile-ladder/`, under the `climb-batch-` name that your brief gives, in the form of the newest one: `summary.txt`, and in `ladder/` the files `ladder.tsv`, `microgpt-phase.md`, `comparison.txt` and `microgpt-comparison.txt`. The next gate compares with the newest summary there or in `explorations/compile-ladder/gate-baseline/`, and finds no other. Land them in a commit that changes nothing else that the gate reads.

Steps 5 and 7 use shell functions that `explorations/coordinator/tools/gate-functions.sh` defines. The file runs nothing. In each Bash call of steps 5 and 7, set up the call as `build-and-caches.md` says, which sets `FORTRESS_HOME` to the tree's root. Then source the file, from the root:

    source explorations/coordinator/tools/gate-functions.sh

## When to run it

Your brief says whether you run the gate. If it does not ask, run only your own tests (`tests-running.md`).

If it asks, first check whether the newest gate still holds for your tree. A gate's tables stay valid until the tree changes under `ProjectFortress/` or `Library/`, or in `build.xml`, outside the test files. A test file is a `.fss`, `.fsi` or `.test` file directly in `ProjectFortress/tests/` or a `ProjectFortress/*_tests/` directory. The commit that landed the newest summary changed nothing that the gate reads. Commit your tree, then run this command. It prints each path, test files excepted, changed since that commit:

    G=$(git log -1 --format=%H -- 'explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/summary.txt')
    git diff --name-only $G HEAD -- ProjectFortress Library build.xml \
        | grep -v -E '^ProjectFortress/([^/]*_)?tests/[^/]*\.(fss|fsi|test)$'

- If it prints a path, run the gate.
- If not, the newest gate holds. Run only the changed test files, through `harness-one.sh` and `junit.sh` (`tests-running.md`).

## The steps

Run these steps from the tree's root. Keep the logs of steps 2 and 4 in `tmp/gate/`, as `compileAll.txt`, `testFast.txt`, `testSystem.txt` and `testSpecData.txt`.

1. Read the Avail column of `df -h /`. Warning: deleting `/tmp/fortress*rats` can break other live runs. If the column shows less than 1 GB, delete `/tmp/fortress*rats`, `ProjectFortress/test-tmp` and `ProjectFortress/test-caches`, and read it again. If it still shows less than 500 MB, stop and report.
2. Run `rm -rf ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS tmp/gate && mkdir -p tmp/gate`, then `ant compileAll`.
3. If the build printed `Caches <tree>/default_repository/caches started again, empty`, run the library order (`build-and-caches.md`). If not, and a source of the compiler's library changed since the caches were filled, take its step in `build-and-caches.md`, "After an edit of the library". Then copy the caches twice for the ladder regression, before anything else compiles into them:

       D=$PWD/tmp/gate/ladder ; mkdir -p $D/root
       cp -a default_repository/caches $D/root/ladder-caches
       cp -a default_repository/caches $D/root/pristine

4. Run `ant testFast`, then `ant testSystem`, then `ant testSpecData`. All three must have zero failures.
5. Write the summary: `gate_summary tmp/gate tmp/gate/summary.txt`. Compare it: `gate_compare "$(last_landed_summary)" tmp/gate/summary.txt`. It prints a line for a suite with failures or errors, a suite with no tests, a suite whose count of tests fell, and a suite that is gone. Each such line makes the gate red. A count that rose prints nothing.
6. Do the atomic runs, and append their lines to the summary.
7. Do the ladder regression.

## The atomic runs

The atomic runs compile fourteen programs, and run each one three times at four threads, in about a minute. They need the library's jars in the tree's caches (`build-and-caches.md`). Run them from `ProjectFortress/`:

    for p in AtomicTopLevelObjectVar AtomicTopLevelVar MutableTopLevelVarInLoop FirstLoadThreadsRungG \
             atomic0 atomic1 atomic2 atomic3 atomic4 atomic5 atomic6 \
             nestedTransactions0 nestedTransactions1 nestedTransactions2 ; do
      d=other_compiler_tests ; [ -f compiler_tests/$p.fss ] && d=compiler_tests
      timeout -k 5 300 ../bin/fortress compile $d/$p.fss >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "# atomic $p COMPILE-FAILED" ; continue ; }
      for i in 1 2 3 ; do
        out=$(FORTRESS_THREADS=4 timeout -k 5 120 ../bin/fortress run $p 2>&1) ; rc=$?
        [ $rc -eq 124 ] && { out=$(FORTRESS_THREADS=4 timeout -k 5 120 ../bin/fortress run $p 2>&1) ; rc=$? ; }
        case "$out" in *FAIL*) r=FAIL ;; *PASS*) r=PASS ;; *) r="NO-PASS rc=$rc" ;; esac
        [ $rc -eq 124 ] && r=TIMEOUT-TWICE
        echo "# atomic $p run$i threads=4 $r"
      done
    done

The gate is red on any FAIL, NO-PASS, COMPILE-FAILED or TIMEOUT-TWICE.

## The ladder regression

The compile ladder records how far each test program gets through the compiler's phases, in order: parse, disambiguate, typecheck, codegen, link, run and pass. The ladder regression runs part of it again, and compares the result with the baseline, `explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/`:

- It compiles and runs the 85 programs of the baseline's `pass-list.txt`. It compares each one's phase and output with the baseline's `raw/`.
- It compiles the eighteen components of the two microGPT programs, and never runs them. It compares each one's phase with the baseline's `microgpt-phase.md`.

A file that moved gets a mark:

- DOWN: a phase lower than the record.
- MISSING: a file with no output.
- STDOUT: output that differs from the record after the `Operation took <n>ms` line is masked.
- UP: a phase higher than the record. This is progress, not red.

DOWN, MISSING and STDOUT are red, unless your brief declared that move as expected before the gate ran.
Warning: do not run `run-ladder.sh`, the driver over every test program, with its defaults. Its default root is shared, its cache pruning corrupts a parallel run, and its default `OUT` is a tracked folder.

To run it, as step 7, with step 3's copies of the caches:

1. Copy the drivers into `tmp/gate/ladder/`, and point their outputs and caches there:

       D=$PWD/tmp/gate/ladder ; B=explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19
       cp explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/run-subset.sh \
          $B/classify.py $B/microgpt-phase.sh $B/microgpt-phase.py $D/
       sed -i -e "s|^OUT=.*|OUT=$D|" -e "s|^LADDER_ROOT=.*|LADDER_ROOT=$D/root|" $D/run-subset.sh
       sed -i -e "s|/home/user/fortress|$PWD|g" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_CACHES=.*|export LADDER_CACHES=$D/root/ladder-caches|" \
           -e "s|^export LADDER_TMP=.*|export LADDER_TMP=$D/root/ladder-tmp|" \
           -e "s|^RAW=.*|RAW=$D/raw/microgpt|" -e "s|^TSV=.*|TSV=$D/microgpt-results.tsv|" $D/microgpt-phase.sh
       tail -n +2 $B/pass-list.txt | cut -f1 | sed 's|/|\t|' > $D/subset.txt

2. Run the four scripts, with no arguments, in this order: `bash $D/run-subset.sh`, `python3 $D/classify.py`, `bash $D/microgpt-phase.sh` and `python3 $D/microgpt-phase.py`. Each reads and writes in `$D`. This takes about 200 s for the 85 and 35 s for the eighteen, so run them in the background (`session.md`, "Long commands"). With step 3's copies, the driver skips the library's build (about 145 s).
3. Compare: `ladder_compare $B $D`, then `diff <(mg_phases $B/microgpt-phase.md) <(mg_phases $D/microgpt-phase.md)`. Append each line that they print to the summary, with `# ladder ` before it.

If your brief asks for your change's own ladder subset, write your own `subset.txt`. Put in it each file whose recorded first error in the baseline's `raw/` names something that your change touched. Run them after your edit only. Compare them with the newest landed `ladder.tsv`, or with the baseline's `raw/` for a file that the gate does not run.

## Comparing with an earlier run

- `ant testSystem` runs in four shards, the summary's rows `system-0` to `system-3`. A shard takes the files by their place in a sorted list, so an added file moves every later file to another shard. When you compare by hand, compare only the sum of the four. `gate_compare` sums them.
- In printed output, mask only these differences: the `Operation took <n>ms` line, a Java line number in a stack frame, an object's identity hash (`@` and hex digits), and a position in a library file that your change moved. In your report, list each test with a masked difference, and the kinds masked in it.
- If your brief asks you to compare the interpreter tests with a base run, use the two scripts in `explorations/coordinator/tools/count-run/`. `count-run.sh` runs every `ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss` under walk, one JVM per test: run it once on the base commit and once after your edit. `compare-normalised.py` compares the two runs, with the last three masks above. Each script's header gives its usage.

== Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1725-1792

\subsection{Shifts and narrowing on the integer types}
\seclabel{revival-shifts}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected sections] \secref{basic-integers}; the overview of operators in
\chapref{operators}.
\item[Change] Two paragraphs after the coercions of \secref{basic-integers} state
the method \VAR{narrow} and the operators \OPR{LSHIFT} and \OPR{RSHIFT}, which this
working draft did not name: \VAR{narrow} keeps the low 32 bits of a value of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} or \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}; on a fixed-size type the
two operators lose the bits shifted out, give \EXP{0}, or \EXP{-1} for a negative
value shifted right, at a count at or beyond the width, and shift the other way for
a negative count; on \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} they are \VAR{shift}; the count may be of any
integer type and is read by its value.
The entry of \VAR{shift} adds that the result is exact for a count of any size and
that a result too large for the implementation throws \TYP{IntegerOverflow}, and
that \OPR{LSHIFT} and \OPR{RSHIFT} compute the same shift on \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}.
The overview of operators names \OPR{LSHIFT} and \OPR{RSHIFT} beside the bitwise
operators.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; the revival decided it on
22~September 2026, with two further decisions on 24~September: that the signed
\VAR{narrow} truncates too, and that \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}'s shifts take a count of any
integer type.
\Library\ declare \OPR{LSHIFT} and \OPR{RSHIFT} on every integer type with a count of
any integer type (\nolinkurl{Library/FortressLibrary.fsi}, lines 459--460), and
\VAR{narrow} on \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} and \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}
(lines 506, 594 and 608), and this working draft said nothing of them.
In the languages the revival compared a shift is an operation on bits whose bits
shifted out are lost, and the revival kept it one on the fixed-size types, with an
exact arithmetic shift on \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} under the name \VAR{shift}, which this
working draft already defines.
For a count at or beyond the width the rule is the one the team's interpreter has
followed since 2007 and three of its gated tests assert
(\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/tests/BitTwiddle.fss}, lines 33, 36 and 39;
\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/tests/UnsignedTest.fss}, lines 30, 32, 135 and 137;
\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/tests/QuickCheckTest.fss}, lines 97--103).
Nothing pinned a negative count; it shifts the other way, and the count is read by
its value, so that a large unsigned count is not read as a negative one.
\VAR{narrow} keeps the low 32 bits as the team's own test asserts at the values
\EXP{2^{64}-1} and \EXP{2^{63}} (\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/tests/UnsignedTest.fss},
lines 210--211), on the signed types as on the unsigned.
The full reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-integer-rules/decision-record.md}
in the revival's repository.
\item[Effect] A count at or beyond the width, or a negative count, has a specified
result, and so has \VAR{narrow} of a value that does not fit.
Both implementations of the revival compute these results on \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} for a count of the shifted value's own type, and the interpreter
on all five types for a count of any integer type; the compiled path, which until it
is built on \library\ compiles against a smaller library of its own, declares
\OPR{LSHIFT} and \OPR{RSHIFT} on \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} only, with
a count of the shifted value's own type, and neither \VAR{narrow} on
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} nor \VAR{shift} (rows~381, 383 and~442 of the revival's gap ledger).
\item[Original text] None for the two paragraphs and for the sentence of the
overview: no chapter of this working draft names \OPR{LSHIFT}, \OPR{RSHIFT} or
\VAR{narrow}.
The entry of \VAR{shift},
\nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex}, lines 698--702,
which the revision keeps and extends:
\begin{quote}
The result of \EXP{\VAR{shift}(x,k)} is \EXP{\lfloor x \cdot 2^k \rfloor}.
This corresponds to what is sometimes called an ``arithmetic shift''
on the two's-complement representation of the integer;
positive values of \VAR{k} shifts the bits to the left,
and negative values of \VAR{k} shifts the bits to the right.
\end{quote}
\item[Route C] The same under route~C.
\end{description}

### 2.3 A call on a type that lacks the member

No name is declared on all five types. So a call on a type without the member goes by coercion to another type's member, or fails (row 859). Run W ran again the three calls whose route crosses a member that batch 24 moved [1]:

- `unsigned` of the `NN32` 2^32 - 1 gives the `NN64` 4294967295. It goes through `ZZ64`'s coercion from `NN32` and then `ZZ64`'s `unsigned`, so `unsigned` here widens.
- `big` of the `NN32` 2^32 - 1 gives the `ZZ` 4294967295, through `ZZ64`.
- `widen` of the `NN64` 2^64 - 1 gives the `ZZ64` -1. It goes through `ZZ`'s coercion from `NN64` and then `ZZ`'s `widen`: a silent change of sign (row 858).

The three refusals are the evidence's, and their ground has not changed: `narrow` of an `NN32` is an "Ambiguous coercion" among three `narrow`s, and `big` of an `NN64` or a `ZZ` finds no overload [7].

The 13 pairs that can lose the value still have 8 members and 5 gaps: no member converts `ZZ32` to `NN64`, `ZZ64` to `NN32`, `NN64` to `ZZ32`, `ZZ` to `NN32` or `ZZ` to `NN64` [8]. A gap is written as two conversions, and for a widening with a change of sign the order changes the value. `unsigned(widen(x))` of the `ZZ32` -1 is 2^64 - 1, the low 64 bits; `widen(unsigned(x))` is 2^32 - 1 [8].

### 2.4 The compiler's prelude

The prelude has not changed since the evidence: `git log --since=2026-10-31` over `CompilerBuiltin.fss` and `.fsi` prints nothing. Its members, in `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss` [9]:

- `ZZ64`: the coercions from `IntLiteral` and `ZZ32` (:579-580); the getter `asZZ32() = jLongOverflowingToInt(self)` (:581), which **raises**; the getter `asZZ` (:582), exact; the getter `bitsAsNN64` (:583), which keeps the bits; `narrow` (:659), which keeps the low bits; `unsigned` (:660), which keeps the bits.
- `ZZ32`: the getters `asZZ32 = self`, `asZZ64 = self` typed `ZZ32` and missing from the api, `asZZ` and `bitsAsNN32` (:665-668); `widen` and `unsigned` (:750-751).
- `NN32`: the getters `asNN32`, `asZZ` and `bitsAsZZ32` (:756-758); `widen` and `signed` (:815-816).
- `NN64`: the coercion from `NN32` (:821); the getters `asNN64`, `asZZ` and `bitsAsZZ64` (:822-824); `narrow` and `signed` (:879-880).
- `ZZ`: coercions from the four fixed widths and `IntLiteral` (:518-522), and no conversion out (row 349; Run Z).
- The prelude imports three forms of each narrowing native: Overflowing, Wrapping and Saturating (:40, :51, :58 for `long` to `int`; :88, :96, :103 for `long` to unsigned `int`). It binds no Saturating one [9].

The checked helper behind `asZZ32` raises where the narrowed value differs from the argument (`simpleIntArith.java:106-110`) [2]. The unsigned one, `longOverflowingToUnsignedInt`, raises when any of the high 32 bits is set (`simpleUnsignedIntArith.java:25-29`, `:87-89`) [2].

component IntLiteralValue
export Executable

(*) The object IntLiteral converts into each number type at a typed binding, equals a zero of another type, takes its own declarations, and its own + answers as today's interpreter gives it.

shown(v: Any): String =
  typecase v of
    IntLiteral => v.asString || " : IntLiteral"
    ZZ32 => v.asString || " : ZZ32"
    ZZ64 => v.asString || " : ZZ64"
    NN32 => v.asString || " : NN32"
    NN64 => v.asString || " : NN64"
    ZZ => v.asString || " : ZZ"
    QQ => v.asString || " : QQ"
    RR64 => v.asString || " : RR64"
    else => v.asString || " : another type"
  end

run(): () = do
    x = IntLiteral
    z: ZZ32 = x
    assert(shown(z), "0 : ZZ32", "literals.tex, section \"Literals\": the libraries define a coercion from the numeral type IntLiteral to ZZ32; IntLiteral at a ZZ32 binding is the ZZ32 zero")
    w: ZZ64 = x
    assert(shown(w), "0 : ZZ64", "literals.tex, section \"Literals\": the libraries define a coercion from the numeral type IntLiteral to ZZ64; IntLiteral at a ZZ64 binding is the ZZ64 zero")
    g: ZZ = x
    assert(shown(g), "0 : ZZ", "literals.tex, section \"Literals\": the libraries define a coercion from the numeral type IntLiteral to ZZ; IntLiteral at a ZZ binding is the ZZ zero")
    q: QQ = x
    assert(shown(q), "0 : QQ", "literals.tex, section \"Literals\": the libraries define a coercion from the numeral type IntLiteral to QQ; IntLiteral at a QQ binding is the QQ zero")
    u: NN32 = x
    assert(shown(u), "0 : NN32", "literals.tex, section \"Literals\": the libraries define a coercion from the numeral type IntLiteral to NN32; IntLiteral at an NN32 binding is the NN32 zero")
    v: NN64 = x
    assert(shown(v), "0 : NN64", "literals.tex, section \"Literals\": the libraries define a coercion from the numeral type IntLiteral to NN64; IntLiteral at an NN64 binding is the NN64 zero")
    r: RR64 = x
    assert(shown(r), "0.0 : RR64", "conversions-coercions.tex, section \"Principles of Coercion\": an integer numeral converts to RR64 by coercion; IntLiteral at an RR64 binding is the RR64 zero")
    assert(x = widen(0), "pins the library: ZZ64 coerces from IntLiteral, so IntLiteral's = at ZZ64 makes IntLiteral equal to the ZZ64 zero")
    assert(even(x) AND NOT odd(x), "pins the library: IntLiteral's own even and odd find the object IntLiteral even")
    assert(shown(floor(x)) || " " || shown(ceiling(x)) || " " || shown(truncate(x)), "0 : IntLiteral 0 : IntLiteral 0 : IntLiteral", "pins the library: IntLiteral's own floor, ceiling and truncate give the object IntLiteral itself")
    assert(x^x = 1, "basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^: a power 0 gives 1 even when the base is 0; the object IntLiteral to the power IntLiteral is 1")
    assert((x.zero = 0) AND (x.one = 1), "pins the library: IntLiteral's own zero and one are 0 and 1")
    assert(shown(x + x), "0 : ZZ32", "pins today's interpreter: IntLiteral's own + answers a ZZ32")
    println "PASS"
  end

end

(* On the compiled path, a builtinPrimitive body whose string names a static helper of nativeHelpers compiles into a call of that helper, self first for a method. *)
component NativeHelperBindingCompiled
export Executable

less(a:ZZ32, b:ZZ32):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intLT")

trait Shape
  same(self, other:Shape):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.equality.sEquiv")
  sameAs(other:Shape, self):Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.equality.sEquiv")
end

object Box(v:ZZ32) extends Shape
  kind():JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.stringOps.typeName")
end

add(a:ZZ32, b:ZZ32):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intOverflowingAdd")

bazS(s:JavaString):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleOverload.baz")
bazI(n:ZZ32):JavaString = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleOverload.baz")

run():() = do
  assert(less(1, 2), "less(1, 2)")
  assert(NOT less(3, 2), "less(3, 2)")
  b = Box(3)
  c = Box(4)
  assert(same(b, b), "same(b, b)")
  assert(NOT same(b, c), "same(b, c)")
  assert(sameAs(b, b), "sameAs(b, b)")
  assert(NOT sameAs(c, b), "sameAs(c, b)")
  assert(b.kind() = "Box", "b.kind()")
  assert(add(2, 3), 5, "add(2, 3)")
  r: ZZ32 := 0
  try
    r := add(2147483647, 1)
  catch e
    IntegerOverflow => r := 1
  end
  assert(r, 1, "add(2147483647, 1) raises IntegerOverflow")
  assert(bazS("x".asJavaString) = "baz x", "bazS")
  assert(bazI(7) = "baz 7", "bazI")
  println("PASS")
end

end

n64Narrow(a:ZZ64):ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleUnsignedIntArith.longWrappingToUnsignedInt")

overflows(f: () -> ZZ64): Boolean =
  try
    ignore f()
    false
  catch e
    IntegerOverflow => true
    Exception => false
  end

dividesByZero(f: () -> ZZ64): Boolean =

  assert(n64Add(n63, n32) = -9223372032559808512, "Add past the signed half, 2^63+2^32 carried in a ZZ64")

scientificHelper(number:RR64):String = do

        power = |\exponent/|
        sign = if power >= 0 then "+" else "-" end
        tens = |\(|power|)/|
        if number < 1 AND number > -1 then

            if bits >= 4463067230724161536 (* (1023-32) 2^52 *) then
                bits := ((bits RSHIFT 20) BITAND 4294967295 (* 2^32-1 *)) - 2147483648 (* 2^31 *)
                exit loop with narrow(bits)
            end
        end

    var state: N = seed MOD modulus

    reseed(seedvec:Indexed[\N,ZZ32\]): LinearCongruential[\N\] =
        do state := seedvec[0] MOD modulus; self end

    random(): N =
        do state := ((mult DOTTIMES widen(state)) DOTPLUS add) MOD modulus; state end

    perturbed(perturbvec:Generator[\ZZ32\]): LinearCongruential[\N\] = do
        (*) XXX Not statistically tested!
        newseed: N := state
        for p <- seq(perturbvec) do
            newseed := ((mult DOTTIMES widen(newseed BITXOR p)) DOTPLUS add) MOD modulus
        end
        state_old = state
        state := (1812433253 (state BITXOR (state RSHIFT 30)) + 1) BITAND 4294967295 (* 2^32-1 *)
        state_old
    end

    perturbed(perturbvec:Generator[\ZZ32\]): MersenneTwisterInit = do
        (*) XXX Not statistically tested!
        newseed: ZZ64 := state
        for p <- seq(perturbvec) do
            newseed := (1812433253 widen(newseed BITXOR p) + 1) BITAND 4294967295 (* 2^32-1 *)
        end
    (* XXX the current implementation requires the range of N is greater than
       the range of T *)
    generate[\N extends Integral[\N\]\](gen:RandomGen[\N\]): T = do
        spacing = (gen.max.get - gen.min.get + 1) DIV |range|
        retrybound = gen.min.get + |range| spacing
        x: N := gen.random()
        while x >= retrybound do x := gen.random() end
        range[narrow((x - gen.min.get) DIV spacing)]
    end

trait CompactFullScalarRange extends { FullScalarRange, CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\] }
    getter stride(): ZZ32 = 1
    getter size(): ZZ32 = do
        l = self.lower
        r = self.upper
        if l > r then 0 else narrow(r-l+1) end
      end
    getter isEmpty(): Boolean = self.lower > self.upper

trait StridedFullScalarRange
        extends { FullScalarRange, StridedFullRange[\ZZ32\] }
    getter size(): ZZ32 =
        if self.isEmpty then 0

    getter isEmpty(): Boolean =
        if self.stride > 0 then (self.left.get>self.right.get)
        TestContext(arbitrary, g', numTests, maxTests, size)

    (** Generates a `ZZ32` value uniformly from the current random number
        generator. It is most suitable for the implementation of `Gen[\ZZ32\]`. **)
    random(): ZZ32 =

(* NN64's operators and narrow bound to nativeHelpers keep their values, their wraparound and their IntegerOverflow under walk. *)
component NativeHelperFamilyNN64Walk
export Executable

overflows(f: () -> NN64): Boolean =
  try
    f()
    false
  catch e
    IntegerOverflow => true
  end

run():() = do
  m: ZZ64 = -1
  lo: ZZ64 = -9223372036854775807 - 1
  z0: ZZ64 = 0
  z1: ZZ64 = 1
  z7: ZZ64 = 7
  z32: ZZ64 = 4294967296
  n0 = unsigned(z0)
  n1 = unsigned(z1)
  n7 = unsigned(z7)
  n32 = unsigned(z32)
  n63 = unsigned(lo)
  nmax = unsigned(m)
  assert(n63.asString, "9223372036854775808", "2^63")
  assert(nmax.asString, "18446744073709551615", "2^64-1")
  assert(n7 = unsigned(z7), true, "=")
  assert(nmax = nmax, true, "= of 2^64-1")
  assert(nmax = n63, false, "= unequal")
  assert(n0 = n7, false, "= unequal at 0")
  assert(n7 < n32, true, "<")
  assert(n63 < nmax, true, "< above the signed half")
  assert(nmax < n7, false, "< is unsigned")
  assert(n7 < n63, true, "< below and above the signed half")
  assert(n0 < n0, false, "< not")
  assert((-n0).asString, "0", "unary - of 0")
  assert(overflows(fn () => -n7), "unary - of 7 overflows")
  assert(overflows(fn () => -nmax), "unary - of 2^64-1 overflows")
  assert((n7 + n7).asString, "14", "+")
(* NN32's operators and getters bound to nativeHelpers keep their values, their wraparound and their IntegerOverflow under walk. *)
component NativeHelperFamilyNN32Walk
export Executable

overflows(f: () -> NN32): Boolean =
  try
    f()
    false
  catch e
    IntegerOverflow => true
  end

run():() = do
  m: ZZ32 = -1
  lo: ZZ32 = -2147483647 - 1
  n0 = unsigned(0)
  n1 = unsigned(1)
  n7 = unsigned(7)
  n16 = unsigned(65536)
  n31 = unsigned(lo)

overflows(f:() -> ZZ64):Boolean = do
  hit: Boolean := false
  try
    hit := eq64(f(), f())
    hit := false
  catch e
    IntegerOverflow => hit := true
  end
  hit
end

dividesByZero64(f:() -> ZZ64):Boolean = do
  hit: Boolean := false
  try
    hit := eq64(f(), f())
    hit := false
  catch e
    DivisionByZero => hit := true
  end
  hit
end

dividesByZeroZ(f:() -> ZZ):Boolean = do
  hit: Boolean := false
  try
    hit := eqZ(f(), f())
    hit := false
  catch e
    DivisionByZero => hit := true
  end
  hit
end

run():() = do
  mx: ZZ64 = 9223372036854775807
  mn: ZZ64 = sub64(-9223372036854775807, 1)
  m1: ZZ64 = -1
  o1: ZZ64 = 1
  s0: ZZ64 = 0
  s2: ZZ64 = 2
  s6: ZZ64 = 6
  s7: ZZ64 = 7
  t10: ZZ64 = 10
  t12: ZZ64 = 12
  r: ZZ64 = 3037000499
  t32: ZZ64 = 4294967296
  assert(eq64(s7, s7), "ZZ64 =")
  assert(NOT eq64(s7, s6), "ZZ64 = unequal")
  assert(NOT eq64(mn, mx), "ZZ64 = at the bounds")
  assert(lt64(s6, s7), "ZZ64 <")
  assert(NOT lt64(s7, s6), "ZZ64 < not")
  assert(NOT lt64(s7, s7), "ZZ64 < equal")
  assert(lt64(mn, mx), "ZZ64 < at the bounds")
  assert(neg64(s7).asString, "-7", "ZZ64 unary -")
  assert(neg64(mx).asString, "-9223372036854775807", "ZZ64 unary - of the maximum")
  assert(overflows(fn () => neg64(mn)), "ZZ64 unary - of the minimum overflows")
  assert(wrapNeg64(s7).asString, "-7", "ZZ64 unary DOTMINUS")
  assert(wrapNeg64(mn).asString, "-9223372036854775808", "ZZ64 unary DOTMINUS wraps")
  assert(add64(s7, s6).asString, "13", "ZZ64 +")
  assert(add64(sub64(mx, o1), o1).asString, "9223372036854775807", "ZZ64 + to the maximum")
  assert(overflows(fn () => add64(mx, o1)), "ZZ64 + overflows")
  assert(overflows(fn () => add64(mn, m1)), "ZZ64 + overflows below")
  assert(wrapAdd64(s7, s6).asString, "13", "ZZ64 DOTPLUS")
  assert(wrapAdd64(mx, o1).asString, "-9223372036854775808", "ZZ64 DOTPLUS wraps")
  assert(sub64(s6, s7).asString, "-1", "ZZ64 -")
  assert(sub64(add64(mn, o1), o1).asString, "-9223372036854775808", "ZZ64 - to the minimum")
  assert(overflows(fn () => sub64(mn, o1)), "ZZ64 - overflows")
  assert(overflows(fn () => sub64(mx, m1)), "ZZ64 - overflows above")
  assert(wrapSub64(s6, s7).asString, "-1", "ZZ64 DOTMINUS")
  assert(wrapSub64(mn, o1).asString, "9223372036854775807", "ZZ64 DOTMINUS wraps")
  assert(mul64(r, r).asString, "9223372030926249001", "ZZ64 DOT")
  assert(mul64(s7, s6).asString, "42", "ZZ64 TIMES")
  assert(overflows(fn () => mul64(t32, t32)), "ZZ64 DOT overflows")
  assert(overflows(fn () => mul64(mn, m1)), "ZZ64 DOT of the minimum by -1 overflows")
  assert(wrapMul64(s7, s6).asString, "42", "ZZ64 DOTTIMES")
  assert(wrapMul64(t32, t32).asString, "0", "ZZ64 DOTTIMES wraps")
  assert(wrapMul64(mx, s2).asString, "-2", "ZZ64 DOTTIMES wraps the maximum")
  assert(div64(s7, s2).asString, "3", "ZZ64 DIV")
  assert(div64(neg64(s7), s2).asString, "-3", "ZZ64 DIV rounds toward zero")
  assert(div64(mn, s2).asString, "-4611686018427387904", "ZZ64 DIV of the minimum")
  assert(overflows(fn () => div64(mn, m1)), "ZZ64 DIV of the minimum by -1 overflows")

\section{Integers}
\seclabel{basic-integers}

The trait \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} (\STR{ZZ}) encompasses all finite integers,
the results of starting from \EXP{0} and repeatedly adding or subtracting \EXP{1} a finite number of times.

\Library\ also declare four integer types of fixed size.
The five integer types are these:

\begin{tabbing}
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} (\STR{ZZ}) is the set of integers (it coerces from \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, and \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} (\STR{ZZ64}) is the set of integers representable in 64-bit two's-complement form (it coerces from \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} (\STR{ZZ32}) is the set of integers representable in 32-bit two's-complement form.
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{N}64} (\STR{NN64}) is the set of integers representable in 64-bit unsigned binary form (it coerces from \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{N}32} (\STR{NN32}) is the set of integers representable in 32-bit unsigned binary form.
\end{tabbing}

Like every number type, each of them is a subtype of \TYP{Number} and of no other
number type (\secref{basic-rationals}), and each coerces into \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}.
An integer type coerces from each other integer type all of whose values it holds,
as listed above; every other conversion between integer types is written explicitly.

Among the explicit conversions, the method \VAR{narrow} converts a value of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} or \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} to \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and a value of
\EXP{\mathbb{N}64} to \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, by keeping its low 32 bits: the result
is the value of the narrower type that is congruent to the argument modulo
\EXP{2^{32}}.
A value that the narrower type holds is unchanged; any other wraps, and no
\TYP{IntegerOverflow} is thrown.

The operators \OPR{LSHIFT} and \OPR{RSHIFT} shift the bits of an integer of any of
the five types by a count of any integer type, and return a value of the type of
the integer shifted.
On \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, \EXP{x \OPR{LSHIFT} k} is \EXP{\VAR{shift}(x,k)} and
\EXP{x \OPR{RSHIFT} k} is \EXP{\VAR{shift}(x,-k)}.
On a fixed-size type of width \VAR{n}, for a nonnegative count \VAR{k},
\EXP{x \OPR{RSHIFT} k} is \EXP{\lfloor x/2^{k} \rfloor}, and
\EXP{x \OPR{LSHIFT} k} is the value of the type that is congruent to
\EXP{x \cdot 2^{k}} modulo \EXP{2^{n}}: the bits shifted out are lost, and no
\TYP{IntegerOverflow} is thrown.
So a count at or beyond the width gives \EXP{0} for a left shift, and for a right
shift \EXP{0}, or \EXP{-1} if \VAR{x} is negative.
A negative count shifts the other way: \EXP{x \OPR{LSHIFT} (-k)} is
\EXP{x \OPR{RSHIFT} k}, and \EXP{x \OPR{RSHIFT} (-k)} is \EXP{x \OPR{LSHIFT} k}.
The count is read by its value, whatever its type: an \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} count of
\EXP{2^{63}} or more is beyond the width, not negative.
\revision{revival-shifts}{The Working Draft of February 2011 named neither
\VAR{narrow} nor \OPR{LSHIFT} and \OPR{RSHIFT}, which \library\ declare on the
integer types; the two paragraphs above state the rules the revival decided for
them.}

It is often desirable to know that an integer lies in a subset of its type,
such as the positive values or the nonzero values.
As for the rationals, such subsets are not types of their own:
a program tests an integer's sign at run time with the comparison operators.
The integer types hold no infinite value.

Here we present only the trait \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} and its methods.
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} is a commutative ring and is totally ordered.

\emph{Future versions of this specification will include
the exact details of how all this is implemented.}

twelve types, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, the type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}^*} that adds the two

\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} is no longer a subtype of \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}, which coerces from it.

+past U+FFFF, and otherwise the character itself followed by a space and its code
+point, as \txt{'\'e 00e9'} for U+00E9.
+The form with the character and its code was built by the team in 2011, in one
+commit with the parser's rule that reads it, but the list did not name it.
+A printable character written as itself stays legible, where the code alone
+hides it; Python and Swift also write a printable character outside ASCII as
+itself.
+The full reasoning is in
+\nolinkurl{explorations/reviews/char-asexprstring-2026-11-06.md} in the
+revival's repository.
+\item[Effect] The parser already read the form.
+The text of \VAR{asExprString} changes in the interpreter at every code point
+but the printable ASCII characters and the five escapes \txt{{\char'134}b},
+\txt{{\char'134}t}, \txt{{\char'134}n}, \txt{{\char'134}f} and
+\txt{{\char'134}r}, and in the compiled path's helper at 2,054 code points: the
+quotation mark, the reverse solidus, U+201C, U+201D, U+2028, U+2029 and the
+2,048 surrogates.
+No code of \library, no test of the suites and no line of the revival's model
+program calls the \VAR{asExprString} of a \TYP{Char}.
+The parser's rule for a code point in hexadecimal digits now tries six digits,
+then five, then four, so that a code of six digits, and in lower case a code of
+five digits whose first four are decimal digits, as \txt{'1000a'}, read as their
+character (row~898 of the revival's gap ledger); every literal that the parser
+read before reads as the same character.
+A surrogate written alone cannot be stored in a source file in UTF-8, so the
+text of a surrogate reads back from a string given to the parser, not from a
+file.
+The parser departs from the text in one case: it
+reads a single 16-bit unit as the character of a character literal, so it
+refuses a character past U+FFFF written as itself, alone or followed by its code
+(row~924); \VAR{asExprString} writes the code alone there.
+The texts are gated by
+\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperFamilyCharWalk.fss} and
+\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyCharCompiled.fss},
+and the forms that they write are read back by
+\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/tests/CharExprStringReadBack.fss}.
+\item[Original text] \nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/lexical-structure.tex},
+lines 861--866:
+\begin{quote}
+The sequence of enclosed characters may be
+a single character
+(e.g., `\txt{a}', \txt{'\$'}, `\txt{$\alpha$}', \txt{`$\oplus$'}),
+a sequence of four or more hexadecimal digits
+identifying the code point of a Unicode character
+(e.g., `\txt{001C}', \txt{`FBAB'}, `\txt{1D11E}'), \ldots
+\end{quote}
+\item[Route C] The same under route~C.

\TYP{UnsignedLong}, forty-one of \TYP{Char}, sixty-two of \TYP{Float} and

\TYP{BigNum}; the thirteen methods of the object \TYP{FlatString} of \library\
and its line separator; the method \VAR{ilkName} of the trait \TYP{Object} and
\EXP{\sequiv} over \TYP{Any}; the four methods of the trait
\TYP{JavaBufferedWriter} and its three factories, over a file's name, standard
output and standard error; and the functions \VAR{char}, \VAR{fromRawBits},
\VAR{nanoTime}, \VAR{random} and \VAR{match}, with \VAR{printThreadInfo},
\VAR{printWithThread}, \VAR{printlnWithThread}, \VAR{getEnvironment} and

23:-Every other conversion between them is explicit, the one into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} written \EXP{\VAR{asFloat}(x)} with the method the library declares on \TYP{Number}.
24:+Every other conversion between them is explicit, the one into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} written \EXP{\VAR{asFloat}(x)} with the method that each number type declares (\secref{revival-asfloat}).
32:+\subsection{The conversion into a float, declared by each number type}
33:+\seclabel{revival-asfloat}
34:+
35:+\begin{description}
36:+\item[Affected sections] \secref{basic-rationals}; \secref{revival-numbers}.
37:+\item[Change] The passage on the conversions between number types says that
38:+the explicit conversion into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64}, \EXP{\VAR{asFloat}(x)}, is the
39:+method that each number type declares, and that \TYP{Number} itself declares
40:+no conversion, where it said that \library\ declare the method on
41:+\TYP{Number}.
42:+The change of \secref{revival-numbers} says the same.
43:+\item[Rationale] The revival decided on 6~November 2026 that \VAR{asFloat}, and
44:+the \EXP{=} that the library built on it, leave the trait \TYP{Number}, and that
45:+each of the library's number types keeps its own \VAR{asFloat}.
46:+The team's later compiler library declares \TYP{Number} with nothing in it
47:+(\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss}, lines
48:+510--511, in the revival's repository), and declares its conversion into
49:+\EXP{\mathbb{R}64} on each of its number types, not on a shared trait; the
50:+Working Draft names no such method.
51:+With \TYP{Number} open to a program's own number types, an abstract
52:+\VAR{asFloat} would oblige a program's complex number to give a float, and an
53:+\EXP{=} on \TYP{Number} built on it would call two different complex numbers
54:+equal.
55:+\Library\ now declare \VAR{asFloat} on \EXP{\mathbb{R}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{R}32},
56:+\EXP{\mathbb{Q}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}32},
57:+\EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} and the numeral type \TYP{IntLiteral}
58:+(\nolinkurl{Library/FortressLibrary.fsi};
59:+\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi}), and the vector
60:+norm at each of the eight number types as its element type.
61:+A reversal would declare \VAR{asFloat} on \TYP{Number} again, abstract, with an
62:+\EXP{=} built on it, so that every type below \TYP{Number} must give a float, or
63:+declare it on a new trait that the number types extend.
64:+\item[Effect] \EXP{\VAR{asFloat}(x)} is unchanged at every number type of the
65:+library.
66:+Two numbers of different types compare by \EXP{=} where a coercion carries one
67:+into the other: for each of the library's 21 coercions between number types,
68:+the type converted to declares \EXP{=} at the type converted from, and that type
69:+declares \EXP{=} at the first, each converting the narrower operand as the
70:+coercion does.
71:+Two numbers of different types that no coercion joins, as a \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}
72:+and an \EXP{\mathbb{R}64}, compare by the library's fallback \EXP{=} over
73:+\TYP{Any}, which answers \EXP{a \sequiv b}; a program that means their values
74:+writes the conversion, \EXP{\VAR{asFloat}(x) = y}.
75:+The interpreter's \EXP{\sequiv} calls numbers of different types equal by value,
76:+so there that fallback answers by value (row~909 of the revival's gap ledger).
77:+A number type of a program's own compares by the \EXP{=} it declares, or else by
78:+the fallback.
79:+\item[Original text] The Working Draft of February 2011 has no such sentence:
80:+the revival added it in its own text of 27~September 2026, not the Working
81:+Draft's.
82:+The passage said, in \nolinkurl{Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex}, lines

input.command:
cd /home/user/fortress-integer-conversions && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex'
s=open(p).read()
old=r"""Among the explicit conversions, the method \VAR{narrow} converts a value of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} or \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} to \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and a value of
\EXP{\mathbb{N}64} to \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, by keeping its low 32 bits: the result
is the value of the narrower type that is congruent to the argument modulo
\EXP{2^{32}}.
A value that the narrower type holds is unchanged; any other wraps, and no
\TYP{IntegerOverflow} is thrown.
"""
new=r"""Among the explicit conversions, each of the five integer types has the getters
\VAR{asZZ32}, \VAR{asZZ64}, \VAR{asNN32}, \VAR{asNN64} and \VAR{asZZ}, which
convert a value to \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \EXP{\mathbb{N}32},
\EXP{\mathbb{N}64} and \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} and keep the value: where the type
converted to does not hold the value, \TYP{IntegerOverflow} is thrown.
The getter to a value's own type returns the value, and a getter to a type that
coerces from the value's type gives the value of the coercion.
Each fixed-size type also has a getter that keeps the bits of a value and reads
them at the same width with the other sign: \VAR{bitsAsNN32} of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \VAR{bitsAsNN64} of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \VAR{bitsAsZZ32} of
\EXP{\mathbb{N}32} and \VAR{bitsAsZZ64} of \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}.

The methods \VAR{narrow}, \VAR{widen}, \VAR{signed}, \VAR{unsigned} and
\VAR{big} also convert, and throw no \TYP{IntegerOverflow}.
The method \VAR{narrow} converts a value of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} to
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and a value of \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} to \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, by
keeping its low 32 bits: the result is the value of the narrower type that is
congruent to the argument modulo \EXP{2^{32}}.
A value that the narrower type holds is unchanged; any other wraps.
The method \VAR{widen} converts a value of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} to
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} and a value of \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} to \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, and
\VAR{big} a value of any integer type to \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}, each keeping the value.
The method \VAR{unsigned} converts a value of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} to
\EXP{\mathbb{N}32} and a value of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} to \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, and
\VAR{signed} converts the other way, each keeping the bits as the getters
\VAR{bitsAsNN32}, \VAR{bitsAsNN64}, \VAR{bitsAsZZ32} and \VAR{bitsAsZZ64} do.
Each of the five methods is declared on every integer type to which it applies,
and returns a value of its result type unchanged: \VAR{narrow} of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and of \EXP{\mathbb{N}32}, \VAR{widen} of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}
and of \EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, \VAR{signed} of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} and of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, \VAR{unsigned} of \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} and of
\EXP{\mathbb{N}64}, and \VAR{big} of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}.
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} has neither \VAR{narrow} nor \VAR{widen}: a value of
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}} converts to a fixed-size type only by a getter.
\revision{revival-int-conversions}{The Working Draft of February 2011 named
none of these conversions, which \library\ declare on the integer types; the
two paragraphs above state the getters and the methods the revival decided for
them, and \VAR{narrow} no longer converts a value of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}}.}
"""
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
old2=r"""\revision{revival-shifts}{The Working Draft of February 2011 named neither
\VAR{narrow} nor \OPR{LSHIFT} and \OPR{RSHIFT}, which \library\ declare on the
integer types; the two paragraphs above state the rules the revival decided for
them.}"""
new2=r"""\revision{revival-shifts}{The Working Draft of February 2011 named neither
\VAR{narrow} nor \OPR{LSHIFT} and \OPR{RSHIFT}, which \library\ declare on the
integer types; the paragraph above states the rules the revival decided for the
shifts, and the paragraph on the methods that keep bits, before it, the rule for
\VAR{narrow} (\secref{revival-int-conversions}).}"""
assert s.count(old2)==1
s=s.replace(old2,new2)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("ok")
EOF
git diff --stat Specification/

## 3. What line 322 does today

    perturb(obj:ZZ, g:AnySeededRandomGen): AnySeededRandomGen =
        if -2147483648 <= obj < 2147483648 then
            g.perturbed(0, narrow(obj))
        else
            perturb(big(widen(obj) LSHIFT 32),
                    g.perturbed(1, narrow((obj BITAND 4294967295 (* 2^32-1 *)) -
                                          2147483648 (* 2^31 *))))
        end

(`Library/QuickCheck.fss:318-326`.)

- The intent: feed the argument into the generator 32 bits at a time, and stop when what is left fits a `ZZ32`.
- **The bug, row 431.** The line shifts left where it should shift right. So only the low 32 bits ever reach the generator.
- Measured (section 7.3): 2^40+7, 2^50+7 and 2^70+7 leave the generator in the same state; 2^40+8 does not. So a random function of a `ZZ` gives one answer for any two large arguments with the same low 32 bits.
- **Which `widen` runs.** The argument is a run-time `ZZ` at every call: 486 of 486 calls in section 7.4. Walk converts a generated `ZZ64` into `ZZ` at the parameter (`fortress-repo` skill, `revival-changes.md`, "Arguments convert"; `ZZ`'s `coerce(x: ZZ64)`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:655`). So line 322 runs `ZZ`'s `widen`, and lines 320 and 323 run `ZZ`'s `narrow`.
- **The values stay within 64 bits.** `genZZ.generate` answered a run-time `ZZ64` 1,000 times in 1,000 (section 7.2). Walk does not convert at a declared return (row 387; `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-flat-tower/REPORT.md:48`).
  - Its levels 8 to 11 (`QuickCheck.fss:301`, `:309-314`) are written to build values beyond 2^64, as `(x LSHIFT 64) BITOR ...`. On a `ZZ64`, the shift loses the bits instead (P-69).
  - The recursion's own value, `big(widen(obj) LSHIFT 32)`, is within 64 bits by construction.
  - The instrumented runs agree: 0 values beyond 64 bits in two runs (`widen-evidence.md`, 8.2).
- Every call of `genZZ.perturb` ends in the in-range branch, at line 320: 200 in-range calls for 200 applications of a random function in section 7.4.

- F-172 **The specification's integer chapter states the library's integer rules.** `narrow` converts a `ZZ64` or `ZZ` to `ZZ32`, and an `NN64` to `NN32`, by keeping the low 32 bits; a value that does not fit wraps, and nothing is thrown. `LSHIFT` and `RSHIFT` work on the five integer types. On `ZZ` they are `shift`, which is exact at any count. On a fixed-size type, `LSHIFT` loses the bits shifted out and throws nothing. `GCD` and `LCM` are nonnegative, and one that a fixed-size type cannot hold throws `IntegerOverflow`. At a negative power, the bases 1 and -1 give their exact power, a base of 0 throws `DivisionByZero`, and any other base throws `IntegerOverflow`. The library follows the same power rule under walk; the compiled path's own library does not (F-263). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-spec-integer-rules/decision-record.md` section 2; `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:39-62` (`narrow` and the shifts) and `:530-542` (the power); `Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:262-268` (`GCD` and `LCM`).
- F-327 **The integers' shifts and powers over `AnyIntegral` convert their count or exponent in Fortress and call public bare bindings at narrow headers.** `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64` and `ZZ` keep `LSHIFT`, `RSHIFT` and `^` over `AnyIntegral` (and `ZZ`'s `shift`) as plain Fortress around a public bare `builtinPrimitive` binding at a `ZZ32` count (`ZZ32`, `NN32`, `ZZ`) or a `ZZ64` count (`ZZ64`, `NN64`) and a `ZZ32` exponent, declared in the api; private functions `shiftCount32`, `shiftCount64`, `powerCount32` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:714-761`) and `countNN32`, `exponentNN32` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:392-420`) keep `Int.shiftCount`'s saturation and `Int.powCount`'s sign and parity, a `ZZ` count or exponent clamped in `ZZ` and then read by `ZZ`'s `narrow`. Ten new helpers and five existing; every value of the walk guard is the glue's. Meaning: the 16 bindings count among F-299's 341, a `ZZ32` count or exponent reaches its bare binding directly, and P-69 and P-153 hold on both paths at these declarations. Test: `tests/NativeHelperShiftPowerWalk`, `compiler_tests/NativeHelperFamilyShiftPowerCompiled`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-natives-shift-power/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why".
- F-124 **On the compiled path, at or beyond the width of `ZZ32` or `ZZ64`, `LSHIFT` gives 0 and `RSHIFT` the sign; both reverse on a negative count, and `narrow` keeps the low 32 bits.** "The sign" is 0 for a nonnegative value and -1 for a negative one. `ZZ64`'s and `NN64`'s `narrow` to 32 bits keeps the low 32 bits. `<<`, `>>` and `<<<` keep their own rules, and `asZZ32` throws out of range. Negation, absolute value and division overflow only at the minimum value and test exactly for it, so the minimum raises `IntegerOverflow`, and `|0|`, `-0` and `0 DIV -1` answer 0. Addition and subtraction test the sign bits, and multiplication computes the exact product (`Math.multiplyExact` on `ZZ64`, a range-checked 64-bit product on `ZZ32`). So these raise `IntegerOverflow` on every overflow, and a zero factor answers 0. `ZZ`'s `<<<` raises a catchable `IntegerOverflow` on a shift that it cannot represent (row 386). content.content:
### 3.2 The library as the team wrote it

`git blame` on today's lines stops at a parentless snapshot of 2012 (`^5a68404fd`), because the conversion of the history cut its parent links. That snapshot's author field names no one who wrote these lines [7]. The authors below are the evidence's reconstruction, which searched the earlier history and the snapshots [8]. The lines of the revival are those that `git blame` gives to "Claude" [1].

- **`ZZ64` to `ZZ32`, `narrow`.** Present in the record's first commit, `72ae6881b` (2007-01-04, the account `jm143038`, Jan-Willem Maessen). It was bound to `Int$FromLong`, which called `Int.rc`, and `Int.rc` threw "Overflow of ZZ32" [9]. It stayed checked, with an error that ends the run, to the team's last commit `a874948ac`. The revival made the error catchable (`413f36ac0`, row 347), and then made it keep the low 32 bits (`d6faad28f`, 2026-09-24), by P-72 [8].
- **`NN64` to `NN32`, `narrow`; `NN32`'s `widen`; `signed` and `unsigned`.** Guy Steele, `dc41d5000` (2008-07-21, his first commit, which added `NN32`, `NN64` and `QQ`). They keep the low bits or the bits. His test asserts the low 32 bits of 2^64 - 1 and 2^63 (`ProjectFortress/tests/UnsignedTest.fss:210-211`) and that `signed` of 2^64 - 1 is below `signed` of 0 (`:219`) [8].
- **`ZZ32`'s `widen`.** In the first commit. Maessen's doc comment of 2008: "widen converts a ZZ32 into a valid ZZ64 quantity." [10]
- **`ZZ64`'s `big`.** Christine Flood, `25acd32f7` (2008-07-10) [8].
- **`ZZ`'s `narrow` and `widen`.** The account Crink, `e1567d62f` (2009-09-10): "Added methods to ZZ to convert to ZZ32 or ZZ64. The nomenclature needs work, in my opinion. Incidentally, my first ever use of Java." Reverted the same day (`02e648434`) and put back the next day (`8d2eb48f5`), unchanged to `a874948ac`, with the comment at fss:1082 [8] [11]. The history records no review. The record leaves open whose account Crink is: "likely external SCA contributor" (`research/authorship.md:68`) [10].
- **`ZZ32`'s `narrow` and `big`, `ZZ64`'s `widen`, and every coercion between integer types**: the revival, `d846e3644` (2026-09-27), when the types became siblings. Before it, `ZZ32` lay under `ZZ64` under `ZZ` and needed no coercion [8].

So at the team's last commit, walk's library was mixed [12]:

- The signed narrowing, `ZZ64` to `ZZ32`, raised.
- The unsigned narrowing and `ZZ`'s two kept the low bits.
- The changes of sign kept the bits.

### 3.3 The team's later word

P-26 says which of the team's decisions wins: "The team's later decision wins over its earlier one, in a text or in code, where the team made it the language's rule." It adds: "Code counts as a decision where the team built it alike for all its types, or stated its rule in a commit message, a comment or the checker. Code that its author called a stub … serve[s] only the implementation." "Later" is the date of the team's work on the point at issue [13].

The team's later work on conversions is in the compiler's prelude, the type group's library:

- **2009.** Maessen's first `asZZ32` on `ZZ64` called `jLongToInt`, `(int) l`: it kept the low bits (`8bcdc8756`, 2009-08-18) [8].
- **2011.** Steele's `9ce7d8189` (2011-09-08, "New test Integer3 (has try-catch problems)") changed that body [14]:

      -    getter asZZ32(): ZZ32 = jLongToInt(self)
      +    getter asZZ32(): ZZ32 = jLongOverflowingToInt(self)

  The same commit made `+`, `-`, `·`, `DIV`, negation and absolute value on `ZZ32` and `ZZ64` checked. It wrote the Overflowing, Wrapping and Saturating natives together, and bound only the Overflowing one [8]. Rung W later counted 32 plainly named members of the prelude's four integer traits that take an Overflowing native [15]. That is a rule built alike for all the types: the plain name checks.
- **2012.** Steele's snapshot `e177c3e2c` (2012-05-22) first holds the `bitsAs…` getters on the four fixed widths, a family built alike. His `304f2743a` (2012-06-12) added the getter `asZZ` on the four fixed widths [8] [10].
- **At the team's last commit**, the prelude declared no `narrow`, `widen`, `signed` or `unsigned`. Rung W added them in 2026 [8].

So the team's later word is: a checked conversion under the plain `as…` name, the bit pattern under `bitsAs…`, and no Fortress name for the low bits. It moved one conversion from the low bits to a check.

**A correction to the ask.** The ask said: "his own pattern has three forms: `as…` checks and raises, `bitsAs…` gives the bits, and `narrow` and `widen` keep the low bits." The third form is not in Steele's prelude. The low-bits names come from walk's library: Steele's 2008 unsigned `narrow`, Crink's 2009 `ZZ` pair, and your P-72 for `ZZ64` [8] [16]. The rest of that sentence holds.

# Rung V, the integer conversions: record lines

Climb batch 28, rung V (rung-integer-conversions), branch wip/rung-integer-conversions. Code commit 2d49a587, specification commit 227979aa, both on base 157323e51.

## Findings

1. **The five integer types convert by checked getters.** On ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32, NN64 and ZZ the getters asZZ32, asZZ64, asNN32, asNN64 and asZZ keep the value and raise IntegerOverflow where the target type does not hold it, under walk, at every edge that tests/IntegerConversionsWalk.fss asserts (in range, and one past each end that exists). Of the 25: 5 identities (\`= self\`); 7 equal the coercions (ZZ32's asZZ64 \`widen(self)\` and asZZ \`big(self)\`, ZZ64's asZZ, NN32's asZZ64 \`signed(widen(self))\`, asNN64 \`widen(self)\` and asZZ, NN64's asZZ); 13 can raise: 6 Fortress bodies with a sign or range test and \`throw IntegerOverflow\` around the low-bits form (ZZ32's asNN32 and asNN64, ZZ64's asNN64, NN32's asZZ32, NN64's asZZ32 and asZZ64), 5 helper bindings (ZZ64's asZZ32 on simpleIntArith.longOverflowingToInt; ZZ64's and NN64's asNN32 on simpleUnsignedIntArith.longOverflowingToUnsignedInt; ZZ's asZZ64 on the new simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.bigOverflowingToLong and asNN64 on the new bigOverflowingToUnsignedLong) and 2 compositions (ZZ's asZZ32 \`self.asZZ64.asZZ32\` and asNN32 \`self.asNN64.asNN32\`). Evidence: Library/FortressLibrary.fss:771-776, :877-884, :983-995, :1096-1102; ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:430-438; the api lines Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:500-505, :568-573, :644-649, :719-723, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:135-140; the harness run 'OK (2 tests)' of IntegerConversionsWalk and IntLiteralTextWalk at 2026-11-08T02:50:38Z. Meaning: the 20 pairs each have a checked member; a program that needs the bits writes bitsAs… or the low-bits name.

(* Today's behaviour, on which the specification is silent: signed of an NN32 or NN64 above its signed half wraps to a negative value, with no IntegerOverflow. *)
component SignedAboveSignedRangeWalk
export Executable

run():() = do
  m32: ZZ32 = -1
  min32: ZZ32 = -2147483647 - 1
  m64: ZZ64 = -1
  assert(signed(unsigned(m32)), m32, "NN32 signed of 2^32-1")
  assert(signed(unsigned(min32)), min32, "NN32 signed of 2^31")
  assert(signed(unsigned(m64)), m64, "NN64 signed of 2^64-1")
end

end

content.content:
# Rung V: the integer conversions (rung-integer-conversions)

- problem: rows 858 and 859, a low-bits name missing on a type and reached by coercion, and row 502, ZZ's widen keeping the low 64 bits (`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:572`, `:573`, `:557`), measured in `explorations/reviews/integer-conversions-2026-11-06.md:281-332`
- spec: `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:39-45` at 157323e51 (the explicit conversions, narrow's sentence), beside "For integer results, overflow throws an IntegerOverflow." (`Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:155`)
- precedent: QQ's `ceiling` and `truncate`, a test and `throw DivisionByZero` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:635`, `:640`); the prelude's `getter asZZ32(): ZZ32 = jLongOverflowingToInt(self)` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:581`); powerCount32's sign test of `signed(c)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:747-751`); the prelude's `trait IntLiteral` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:883-889`)
- deviation: ZZ's asZZ64 and asNN64 bind two new helpers, `simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.bigOverflowingToLong` and `bigOverflowingToUnsignedLong`, beyond fork V1's three pairs, since after the deletion ZZ has no low-bits form for a Fortress body to wrap (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.java:147-157`)
- deviation: `Library/QuickCheck.fss:322` on `.asZZ64` raises IntegerOverflow for a ZZ outside ZZ64, where `widen` kept the low 64 bits; under walk no generator makes one (row 387) (`Library/QuickCheck.fss:322`)
- deviation: two calls of ZZ's narrow outside the named declarations moved, in countNN32 and exponentNN32 (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:400`, `:419`)
- deviation: the getters stand before each type's methods, which the parser requires: 'Field/getter/setter declarations should come before method declarations.' (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:500`, `:568`, `:644`, `:719`; `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:135`)
- historical: `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi`, `Library/Format.fss`, `Library/QuickCheck.fss`, `ProjectFortress/demos/sudoku.fss`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`, `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.java`, `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex`, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1`)

Commits on `wip/rung-integer-conversions`: 2d49a587 (the code and its tests), 227979aa (the specification). The worktree was seeded by `seed-worktree.sh` (exit 0, 4 s).

## What changed and why

P-161, option 6, whole, and P-169's eight numeral bindings.

**The 25 getters**, each declared in the api at the component's header, each a getter before the type's methods:

| type | asZZ32 | asZZ64 | asNN32 | asNN64 | asZZ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ZZ32 (`FortressLibrary.fss:771-775`, `.fsi:568-572`) | `= self` | `widen(self)` | Fortress, raises below 0 | Fortress, raises below 0 | `big(self)` |
| ZZ64 (`.fss:877-883`, `.fsi:644-648`) | helper `simpleIntArith.longOverflowingToInt` | `= self` | helper `simpleUnsignedIntArith.longOverflowingToUnsignedInt` | Fortress, raises below 0 | `big(self)` |
| NN32 (`FortressBuiltin.fss:430-437`, `.fsi:135-139`) | Fortress, raises at 2^31 and up | `signed(widen(self))` | `= self` | `widen(self)` | `big(self)` |
| NN64 (`.fss:983-994`, `.fsi:500-504`) | Fortress, raises at 2^31 and up | Fortress, raises at 2^63 and up | helper `simpleUnsignedIntArith.longOverflowingToUnsignedInt` | `= self` | `big(self)` |
| ZZ (`.fss:1096-1102`, `.fsi:719-723`) | `self.asZZ64.asZZ32` | helper `simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.bigOverflowingToLong` (new) | `self.asNN64.asNN32` | helper `simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.bigOverflowingToUnsignedLong` (new) | `= self` |

So 5 identities, 7 equal to the coercions (each the coercion's own one-call body), and 13 that can raise: 6 Fortress bodies, a sign or range test and `throw IntegerOverflow` around the low-bits form, as QQ's `truncate` throws `DivisionByZero`; 3 on the existing checked helpers of fork V1; 2 on new helpers; 2 compositions over them. The Java signatures: `public static int longOverflowingToInt(long l)` (`simpleIntArith.java:106`), `public static int longOverflowingToUnsignedInt(long l)` (`simpleUnsignedIntArith.java:87`), and the new `public static long bigOverflowingToLong(BigInteger a)` and `public static long bigOverflowingToUnsignedLong(BigInteger a)` (`simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.java:148`, `:154`), which raise `fortress.CompilerBuiltin$IntegerOverflow` as the other helpers do. Walk carries ZZ in BigInteger, ZZ64 and NN64 in long, NN32 in int; the compiled rewrite passes an NN32 or NN64 result through its transfer helper.

**The four bitsAs getters**: bitsAsNN32 of ZZ32 and bitsAsNN64 of ZZ64 are `unsigned(self)`, bitsAsZZ32 of NN32 and bitsAsZZ64 of NN64 `signed(self)` (`FortressLibrary.fss:776`, `:884`, `:995`; `FortressBuiltin.fss:438`).

**The low-bits names, newly declared** (fork V5, option 1's nine): narrow and unsigned of NN32 `= self`, big of NN32 `big(signed(widen(self)))` (`FortressBuiltin.fss:523-525`, `.fsi:191-193`); widen and unsigned of NN64 `= self`, big of NN64 `do z: ZZ = self; z end` (`FortressLibrary.fss:1075-1077`, `.fsi:555-557`); signed of ZZ32 and of ZZ64 `= self` (`.fss:862`, `:973`; `.fsi:631`, `:706`); big of ZZ `= self` (`.fss:1189`, `.fsi:772`). ZZ has neither narrow nor widen.

**Deleted**: ZZ's narrow and widen, on the glue `BigNum$ToZZ32` and `BigNum$ToZZ64` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1150-1154` and `.fsi:744-745` at 157323e51).

**ZZ32's big** names `simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.makeZZfromZZ32` (`FortressLibrary.fss:860-861`), not the glue `Long$ToBigNum`.

**IntLiteral's 8** (`FortressBuiltin.fss:544-551`, `:557`, `:570-574`), with their api lines unchanged:

    getter asZZ32(): ZZ32 = self.asZZ.asZZ32
    getter asZZ64(): ZZ64 = self.asZZ.asZZ64
    getter asNN32(): NN32 = self.asZZ.asNN32
    getter asNN64(): NN64 = self.asZZ.asNN64
    getter asString(): String = self.asZZ.asString
    getter asExprString(): String = self.asZZ.asString
    opr =(self, b: IntLiteral):Boolean = self.asZZ = b.asZZ
    cmp(b:IntLiteral): ZZ32 = do
        x = self.asZZ
        y = b.asZZ
        if x < y then -1 elif y < x then 1 else 0 end
      end

`asZZ` stays on its glue class, as fork V3 says.

**The callers of ZZ's narrow and widen**, each moved with its value (fork V4), before at 157323e51 and after at 2d49a587:

| site | before | after | why the value fits |
|---|---|---|---|

# Rung V, the integer conversions: record lines

Climb batch 28, rung V (rung-integer-conversions), branch wip/rung-integer-conversions. Code commit 2d49a587, specification commit 227979aa, both on base 157323e51.

## Findings

1. **The five integer types convert by checked getters.** On ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32, NN64 and ZZ the getters asZZ32, asZZ64, asNN32, asNN64 and asZZ keep the value and raise IntegerOverflow where the target type does not hold it, under walk, at every edge that tests/IntegerConversionsWalk.fss asserts (in range, and one past each end that exists). Of the 25: 5 identities (`= self`); 7 equal the coercions (ZZ32's asZZ64 `widen(self)` and asZZ `big(self)`, ZZ64's asZZ, NN32's asZZ64 `signed(widen(self))`, asNN64 `widen(self)` and asZZ, NN64's asZZ); 13 can raise: 6 Fortress bodies with a sign or range test and `throw IntegerOverflow` around the low-bits form (ZZ32's asNN32 and asNN64, ZZ64's asNN64, NN32's asZZ32, NN64's asZZ32 and asZZ64), 5 helper bindings (ZZ64's asZZ32 on simpleIntArith.longOverflowingToInt; ZZ64's and NN64's asNN32 on simpleUnsignedIntArith.longOverflowingToUnsignedInt; ZZ's asZZ64 on the new simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.bigOverflowingToLong and asNN64 on the new bigOverflowingToUnsignedLong) and 2 compositions (ZZ's asZZ32 `self.asZZ64.asZZ32` and asNN32 `self.asNN64.asNN32`). Evidence: Library/FortressLibrary.fss:771-776, :877-884, :983-995, :1096-1102; ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:430-438; the api lines Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:500-505, :568-573, :644-649, :719-723, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fsi:135-140; the harness run 'OK (2 tests)' of IntegerConversionsWalk and IntLiteralTextWalk at 2026-11-08T02:50:38Z. Meaning: the 20 pairs each have a checked member; a program that needs the bits writes bitsAs… or the low-bits name.
2. **The fixed widths' bitsAs getters keep the bits:** bitsAsNN32 of ZZ32 and bitsAsNN64 of ZZ64 are `unsigned(self)`, bitsAsZZ32 of NN32 and bitsAsZZ64 of NN64 are `signed(self)` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:776, :884, :995; FortressBuiltin.fss:438); IntegerConversionsWalk asserts -1 to 2^32-1 and 2^64-1, -2^31 to 2^31, and the reverse.
3. **The low-bits names are declared on every type where they apply, so no call of one goes through a coercion.** New: narrow and unsigned of NN32 (`= self`), big of NN32 (`big(signed(widen(self)))`, the coercion's body), widen and unsigned of NN64 (`= self`), big of NN64 (`do z: ZZ = self; z end`, numerator's form), signed of ZZ32 and of ZZ64 (`= self`), big of ZZ (`= self`) (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:862, :973, :1075-1077, :1189; FortressBuiltin.fss:523-525). Before, unsigned of an NN32 answered an NN64 through ZZ64, widen of the NN64 2^64-1 the ZZ64 -1 through ZZ, narrow of an NN32 was an ambiguous coercion and big of an NN64 or a ZZ found no overload (rows 858, 859). IntegerConversionsWalk asserts each new member. A grep of the library, the tests, the demos and the model for a call of one of these on a type that lacked it found none, and ant testSystem's verdicts are unchanged.
4. **ZZ has no narrow and no widen; it converts to a fixed width only by a getter.** Library/FortressLibrary.fss and .fsi at 157323e51 had them at fss:1150-1154 on the glue BigNum$ToZZ32 and BigNum$ToZZ64. Probes NarrowOfZZ and WidenOfZZ: old code 'narrow: 5' (2^32+5) and 'widen: -9223372036854775808' (2^63); new code 'Failed to find any matching overload, args = (4294967301:ZZ)'. The callers moved, each value the same where the ZZ fits: Library/Format.fss:70, :117, :122; Library/QuickCheck.fss:320, :322, :323-324; ProjectFortress/demos/sudoku.fss:42-43; Library/FortressLibrary.fss:723 (shiftCount32), :754 (powerCount32); ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:400 (countNN32), :419 (exponentNN32); ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXZZNarrowRungP.fss. sudoku's output is the same old and new.
5. **QuickCheck's genZZ.perturb now raises IntegerOverflow for a ZZ outside ZZ64's range, where it kept the low 64 bits.** Library/QuickCheck.fss:322 is `perturb(big(obj.asZZ64 LSHIFT 32), ...)`. The probe of explorations/reviews/quickcheck-widen.md, 7.3, with a catch added, old code: '2^63: 1543497436', '2^70 + 7: 1001751898'; new code: '2^63: IntegerOverflow', '2^70 + 7: IntegerOverflow'; 2^40+7, 2^50+7, 2^40+8, -2^63 and 7 answer as before. Under walk genZZ.generate makes no value beyond 64 bits (row 387), so no gated run reaches it. Row 431's rewrite holds it.
6. **IntLiteral's 8 are Fortress text over its asZZ:** asZZ32, asZZ64, asNN32 and asNN64 `self.asZZ.<getter>`, asString and asExprString `self.asZZ.asString`, `=` at IntLiteral `self.asZZ = b.asZZ`, cmp -1, 0 or 1 by ZZ's < (FortressBuiltin.fss:544-551, :557, :570-574). At the object IntLiteral, tests/IntLiteralTextWalk.fss answers the same on the base and after: '0 : ZZ32', '0 : ZZ64', '0 : NN32', '0 : NN64', asString and asExprString '0', `x = x`, `x <= x`, `x >= x`, `x CMP x` EqualTo, not `x < x`, not `x > x`. ZZ32's big of 2^31-1 and -2^31 answers '2147483647 : ZZ' and '-2147483648 : ZZ' on both, now on makeZZfromZZ32 (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:860-861).
7. **The bindings, by grep of the one library's .fss files, from 157323e51 to 2d49a587:** builtinPrimitive strings 418 to 413, those naming nativeHelpers 340 to 346, the others 78 to 67. So 11 bindings leave glue (ZZ32's big, ZZ's narrow and widen, IntLiteral's 8, two of which named one glue class) and 6 helper bindings come; by F-299's count, 443 live bindings become 438, 341 on helpers 347, and 102 on glue 91.
8. **On the compiled path the five helpers that the getters bind answer as the walk getters do** when bound at the Java types the compile reads: compiler_tests/IntegerConversionHelpersCompiled (link and run, 'OK (3 tests)' with XXXZZNarrowRungP at 2026-11-08T02:50:55Z). It fails on the base: 'builtinPrimitive names no static helper: com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.bigOverflowingToLong'.
9. **The stages on 2d49a587:** the count stage's table equals climb batch 27's (diff prints nothing; #total 0, #crash none); the distance stage's #total 0, and compare.sh prints 'DISTANCE SAME   0' with both crash rows of value object Char 'crash gone'; Char, now FortressBuiltin.fss:669:1-781:2, reads '@@TC DECL-OK ... errors=0'. Row 929's two crash rows go on this tree; the cause is not analysed here.

## FACTS entry

**The integer types convert by checked as… getters that raise IntegerOverflow, bitsAs… getters for the bits, and the low-bits names on every type, and ZZ converts out only by its getters.** On ZZ32, ZZ64, NN32, NN64 and ZZ, asZZ32, asZZ64, asNN32, asNN64 and asZZ keep the value or raise IntegerOverflow: 5 identities, 7 the coercions, 13 that can raise, 8 of them Fortress bodies or compositions and 5 bare helper bindings (simpleIntArith.longOverflowingToInt, simpleUnsignedIntArith.longOverflowingToUnsignedInt twice, simpleArbitraryPrecisionArith.bigOverflowingToLong and bigOverflowingToUnsignedLong). bitsAsNN32, bitsAsNN64, bitsAsZZ32 and bitsAsZZ64 equal unsigned and signed. narrow, widen, signed, unsigned and big keep the bits, each on every type where it applies, the value itself where it is of the result type; ZZ has big only. IntLiteral's asZZ32, asZZ64, asNN32, asNN64, asString, asExprString, = and cmp are Fortress over its asZZ. Meaning: under walk no conversion goes through a coercion and `narrow(z)` of a ZZ finds no declaration (write `z.asZZ32`); by F-299's count the bindings are 438, 347 on helpers and 91 on glue; until the switch-over the compiled prelude has 8 of the 25 getters and no big (row 349). Test: tests/IntegerConversionsWalk, tests/IntLiteralTextWalk, compiler_tests/IntegerConversionHelpersCompiled, compiler_tests/XXXZZNarrowRungP. Detail: compile-ladder/rung-integer-conversions/REPORT.md, "What changed and why".

## FACTS entries made false

- F-172, "The specification's integer chapter states the library's integer rules.": its first sentence says `narrow` converts a ZZ64 or ZZ to ZZ32; now ZZ has no narrow, and the chapter also states the getters (Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:39-79); its line citation `:39-62` is now `:39-98`.
- F-327, "The integers' shifts and powers over AnyIntegral convert …": "a ZZ count or exponent clamped in ZZ and then read by ZZ's narrow" is now read by ZZ's asZZ32 (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:723, :754; FortressBuiltin.fss:400, :419), each value the same.
- F-299, "Walk loads a builtinPrimitive string …": its counts 443, 341 and 102 move as finding 7 gives; its list gains ZZ64's asZZ32 and asNN32, NN64's asNN32, ZZ's asZZ64 and asNN64 and ZZ32's big, and the glue list loses "the conversions 3" and 8 of IntLiteral's 29.

## Ledger

Rows that close with commit 2d49a587 (`ledger.py close N --commit 2d49a587 --test NAME`):

- 858, test `ProjectFortress/tests/IntegerConversionsWalk.fss` (widen of the NN64 2^64-1 is '18446744073709551615 : NN64').
- 859, test `ProjectFortress/tests/IntegerConversionsWalk.fss` (unsigned, narrow and big of NN32, big of NN64 and of ZZ, signed of ZZ32 and ZZ64 each answer on its own type).
- 502, test `ProjectFortress/tests/IntegerConversionsWalk.fss` (ZZ has no widen; asZZ64 of the ZZ 2^63 and 2^64+5 raises IntegerOverflow).
- 856, test `ProjectFortress/tests/IntegerConversionsWalk.fss`: its notes say it closes when the checked asZZ32 and asZZ64 land on NN32 and NN64; they raise at 2^31 and 2^63, and signed keeps the bits, as `tests/SignedAboveSignedRangeWalk.fss` asserts.

Rows rewritten (`ledger.py rewrite N FILE`), each line linted by `ledger.py check --rows` ('2 rows, 0 fail the template'):

Row 349 (its narrow half closed by the deletion; the line states the prelude's gap against the revised chapter, with XXXZZNarrowRungP rewritten for asZZ32):

| 349 | compiled, the prelude has 8 of the 25 checked getters that `basic-integers.tex` states, none on `ZZ`, no `big`, and no `narrow`, `widen`, `signed` or `unsigned` that returns its argument, so `.asZZ32` of a `ZZ`, which walk answers, is refused | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | library gap vs spec (prelude) | `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex`, "Integers" | `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXZZNarrowRungP.test` | climb batch 2 rung W's skeptic | siblings: 442. The 8: `asZZ32` of `ZZ32` and `ZZ64`, `asNN32` of `NN32`, `asNN64` of `NN64`, `asZZ` of the fixed widths (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:150-152`, `:206-207`, `:212-214`, `:269-270`, `:275-277`, `:328-329`, `:335-337`, `:386-387`, at 157323e51); its `trait ZZ` (`:103-145`) has no conversion out. The test compiles `z.asZZ32` of a `ZZ` and is refused: 'ZZ has no getter called asZZ32'. `narrow` of a `ZZ32` 43 compiles by coercion through `ZZ64`'s `coerce(x: ZZ32)` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:580`) and gives 43. Closes at the switch-over (P-37). |

Row 431 (line 322 now reads .asZZ64, which raises beyond ZZ64; the claim narrowed):

| 431 | `genZZ.perturb` in `Library/QuickCheck.fss` recurses on its argument shifted left by 32 where peeling 32 bits at a time needs a right shift, so only a large `ZZ`'s low 32 bits reach the generator, and one outside `ZZ64` raises: under walk it answers 2^40+7 and 2^50+7 alike, and raises at 2^70+7 | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | library bug (library) | silent | none | climb batch 6 rung F | `Library/QuickCheck.fss:322` is `perturb(big(obj.asZZ64 LSHIFT 32), ...)`, which stays within 64 bits and ends; the team's `obj LSHIFT 32` never ends on a `BigNum` (`OutOfMemoryError` in `ReflectiveQuickCheckTest`). Probe of `explorations/reviews/quickcheck-widen.md`, 7.3, with a `catch`: '2^40 + 7: 1001751898', '2^50 + 7: 1001751898', '2^70 + 7: IntegerOverflow'. No test sees it: `genZZ.generate` makes no value beyond 64 bits under walk (row 387). Fix: `perturb(obj RSHIFT 32, ...)`, which changes every QuickCheck test's generated data. full text: history, row 431 |

Row 578 stays as it is (IntLiteral's own arithmetic still answers a ZZ32 under walk).

No new row.

## Handover

Rung V landed P-161 whole and IntLiteral's 8 of P-169: the 25 checked getters, the 4 bitsAs getters and the 9 missing low-bits names on the five integer types, ZZ's narrow and widen deleted with their 12 callers moved onto asZZ32 or asZZ64, ZZ32's big on makeZZfromZZ32, IntLiteral's 8 in Fortress, two new helpers for ZZ's asZZ64 and asNN64, an Appendix I entry; rows 858, 859, 502 and 856 close, 349 and 431 are rewritten; count 0, distance 0 with row 929's two crash rows gone on this tree.

## Revival change
